title: Add debug endpoint/CLI to explain kernel selection decision path ("why this kernel")
creator: Grace Kim
description:
Goal
Build a developer/operator-facing tool to answer: “Why did selector choose kernel X for this request?” for kernel auto-selection v2.

This should reduce time-to-triage for:
- unexpected p95 regressions on specific GPU SKUs / seq-length regimes
- disagreements between expected registry row and observed choice (overrides, fallback, unknown model family)
- correctness investigations (confirm kernel id + safe-set fallback)

Deliverable (two surfaces)
1) Debug endpoint (internal/admin-only) that returns an explanation blob for a given request context.
2) CLI output (same underlying logic) for local repro and for SRE/release triage on canary.

Request context inputs (minimum viable)
- selector_version: v1 | v2 | auto (if auto, show both “available” and “chosen”)
- model: model_id OR explicit model_family + key flags (e.g., GQA) if model_id metadata unavailable
- regime: prefill | decode (or “unknown” if not provided)
- seq bucket: effective_context_tokens_bucket (e.g., 0-256, 257-1k, 1k-4k, 4k-8k, 8k+)
- gpu: normalized sku (L4, A10, A100-80GB, H100, etc.) + compute capability if available
- optional: customer tier/cluster mode (hosted/dedicated/private) ONLY if it influences overrides; do not leak tenant identifiers

Expected output (human-readable + machine-parseable)
- chosen_kernel_id
- selector_version_used (v1/v2)
- registry_version (if v2)
- normalized inputs:
  - resolved model_family + mapping rule that fired (e.g., “metadata.arch=llama + gqa=true => llama-gqa”)
  - resolved gpu_sku + mapping rule (e.g., “NVIDIA_DEVICE=10de:27b8 => L4”)
  - resolved seq bucket + boundary logic used
  - resolved regime (prefill/decode) source
- decision path:
  - override checks (global kill switch, per-model-family pin, per-gpu pin, emergency safe-set)
  - table lookup (row key) + match quality (exact match vs fallback)
  - fallback rationale if not exact (unknown family, missing row, incompatible kernel, safety policy)
  - tie-breaker explanation if multiple candidates (deterministic ordering)
- safety signals:
  - “in_safe_kernel_set=true/false”
  - validation notes if applicable (e.g., “kernel requires sm>=80; current sm=75 so skipped”)

Endpoint details
- Route: /admin/runtime/kernel-selector/explain (name can change; must be clearly ‘admin’/non-public)
- AuthZ: restricted to oncall/SRE + runtime engineers (reuse existing admin auth). No customer access.
- Rate limiting: strict (debug only). Avoid turning this into an online hot path.
- Logging: do not emit raw prompt text, token sequences, or tenant ids. Log only the normalized fields already allowed by telemetry standards.

CLI details
- Command: redwood-runtime debug kernel-choice --model <id> --gpu <sku> --regime <prefill|decode> --seq <n>
- Include a “--json” flag for machine parse.
- Must work in dev environment without calling production services (reads local registry file + uses same mapping rules).

Non-goals
- Not a replacement for metrics dashboards. This is for pinpointing a single context.
- Not a general ‘trace explorer’. We will link the explanation to trace attributes that already exist.
- No customer-facing API/Console surface in this ticket.

Acceptance criteria
- Given a known request context from canary logs, oncall can run CLI and get the same kernel_id as observed in telemetry.
- For an unknown model family, explanation explicitly shows fallback to safe kernel set + why.
- Explanation includes override precedence ordering and clearly indicates which override (if any) changed the choice.
- Endpoint is gated behind admin auth; security sign-off recorded.
- Docs: add a short section to the profiling playbook linking to this tool.

References
- Project: Kernel auto-selection v2 (ENG-3921)
- PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_18507_debug_endpoint_explain_kernel_choice.json
- Profiling playbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/debugging-kernel-selection.json
- Telemetry standards (labels/bucketing): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/kernel-selection-telemetry-standards.json

Open questions
- Should we expose both v1 and v2 decisions in the same output (recommended for rollout triage), or only the active selector?
- Do we need a ‘shape hints’ input (head_dim, kv_heads) for a more precise explanation? (We can defer unless needed for mismatch bugs.)
comments: 2026-01-24 (Grace Kim): Creating this based on repeated asks in runtime sync + Slack thread. During canary we keep debating whether we’re on the expected registry row vs an override/fallback. Would like a single command/output we can paste into threads.

2026-01-28 (Omar El-Sayed): Proposed implementation: expose a pure function explainKernelChoice(ctx) used by both (a) admin endpoint and (b) CLI. It will return a structured object + a pretty printer. Will include explicit override precedence list. Looping in Benji for config/flag wiring assumptions.

2026-02-02 (Thomas Baird): Please ensure endpoint logs do NOT introduce new high-cardinality labels. If we need logging, keep it to the same bucketed fields as selector telemetry (family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket, regime, kernel_id, selector_version). No model_id or raw device name.

2026-02-05 (Connor O’Brien): From Release Eng perspective, CLI is most useful. Endpoint is helpful but we can’t rely on it being accessible everywhere (Dedicated/private). Please prioritize CLI parity and document how to run against a specific registry version (e.g., from runtime build artifact).

2026-02-10 (Omar El-Sayed): Implementation done in PR 18507. Endpoint lives under /admin and requires admin auth. CLI added under redwood-runtime debug kernel-choice with --json and plain output. Added support for ‘--compare v1’ to print both v1 and v2 and highlight divergence.

2026-02-12 (Allison Grant): Security/ops note: endpoint response must not include internal file paths or hostnames. Looks good after latest revision. Please add one sentence to the playbook about who can access the endpoint and when to prefer CLI.

2026-02-14 (Omar El-Sayed): Added doc snippet to profiling playbook and linked from kernel-selection debug section. Verified against A10 long-context regression example: explanation clearly showed per-model-family override forcing a safe kernel. Marking ready for review.
2026-02-18 (Hiro Tanaka): Reviewed output formatting. Request: include registry row key and match type (exact vs fallback) in the pretty output, not just JSON. Approved after change.
2026-02-20 (Omar El-Sayed): Landed + backported to runtime-1.19 branch. Verified on canary host: output matches telemetry kernel_id for sampled requests. Closing.
